title: Restock a twin jumbo-roll tissue dispenser: stub to the reserve spindle, new roll on the primary, cover locked
instruction: This dispenser is almost empty. Restock it with the new roll so the old one gets used up first, and lock it.
context: Restocking restroom dispensers is a core task of janitors and cleaners (O*NET 37-2011.00; 2,172,500 US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2023). On a twin jumbo-roll dispenser the nearly used stub is moved to the reserve spindle so it is finished first, and the new roll goes on the primary; each sprung hub only lets a core on or off while its release tab is held, and the cover only closes once its stay is released. The instruction says none of this.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the bench top. Dispenser lying on its back, front up: white back plate 30 (x) x 49 (y) x 0.6 cm at x 13.5-43.5, y -24.5 to 24.5, with a 3 cm rim (0.4 cm walls). Two spindles, primary at x 29.65, y 12 and reserve at x 29.65, y -12: each a 2 x 2 x 0.08 cm bearing boss on the back plate carrying a grey split hub (40 g) that turns freely on it about the boss's centre (bearing drag 0.05 N*m*s/rad), so a loaded roll spins. The hub is 3 cm tall, measured from a reference 2.15 cm -x of the boss: a fixed half (1.5 x 2.4 cm, 0.1-1.6 cm on the -x side of the reference) and a sprung half (1.1 x 2.4 cm, 20 g, 500 N/m, 4.8 cm travel) 5.1-6.2 cm on the +x side of it, which blocks a 7.5 cm core unless drawn in and pushes a seated core +x against the fixed half. Release tabs: blue 1.4 cm buttons (20 g, 400 N/m, 6 mm travel) on 1.8 cm bosses, primary's at x 15, y 1.5, reserve's at x 15, y -1.5; pressed 4 mm or more, that hub's sprung half draws in. Slide gate: red lever 8 x 1.2 x 0.8 cm (30 g) on a post at x 29, y -21.5, 3.9 cm up, lying over the reserve hub (pointing +y), detents at 0 and 90 deg clockwise (clear). Stub: 12-sided paper ring, 8.3 cm across, 7.5 cm core, 9 cm tall, 150 g, seated on the primary hub. New roll: 23 cm across, 7.5 cm core, 9 cm tall, 0.9 kg, on the bench at x 30, y 40. Cover: smoked shell 30 x 49 x 7.4 cm, 0.5 kg, with two tissue outlet windows in its front panel, 1 to 6.5 cm in from the hinge edge: reserve window y -20 to -4, primary window y 4 to 20, hinged along the far rim (x 43.5, 3.6 cm up) with a closing spring (0.5 N*m/rad) and a 3 N*m*s/rad damper; it starts open at 100 deg, held by a stay. A red changeover shutter (7.3 x 17 x 0.3 cm, 20 g) slides along the outside of the front panel with detents over the primary window (as set, so tissue is drawn from the stub first) and 24 cm toward the reserve window. Stay release: blue 1.6 cm button on a 2.4 x 2.4 x 3 cm grey post at x 25, y -28. Waste bin: dark 11 x 11 x 5 cm open box at x 10, y 40.
scoring: Seated: core bottom within 3 mm of the back plate, its axis within 25 mm of the hub's middle (2.25 cm -x of the bearing boss; any further off, the core wall would sit up on the hub) and within 3 deg of vertical. A core counts as engaged only if its hub's sprung half was drawn in (tab held) while the core was down over that spindle, and now rests against the core (held 0.5 to 3.6 cm in). Points: stub seated and engaged on the reserve hub, its axis within 6 mm of where the sprung half pushes it (on the bearing boss's axis), and the gate clear (80 deg or more) 0.3; only with that: new roll seated and engaged on the primary hub 0.3; only with both: cover shut (after the stay is released, by its spring and damper or by hand) (under 1 deg) and latched (the latch clicks under 1.5 deg) 0.3, then no gripper within 2 cm of either roll, a tab or the stay button, with rolls and cover still (under 1 cm/s, 0.25 rad/s) 0.1. Score 0 if the run ends with the stub outside the dispenser (bench, bin or hand) or the new roll on the reserve and the stub on the primary. Score 0, latched, if the cover is slammed: still closing at over 6 rad/s within 15 deg of shut, so its front edge meets the rim at over 1.8 m/s (spring and damper alone close it at about 0.3 rad/s; closing it by hand at up to 5 rad/s is fine), a roll falls 5 cm below the bench, the stub goes into the bin, or the cover comes down within 45 deg onto a core inside the dispenser that is not seated. Scored at the last step; 1.0 held for 1 s ends the run.
reset_notes: Open the cover to 100 deg and set its stay (press the latch), hold the reserve tab and take the stub off, put it back on the primary (tab held), take the new roll off and lay it at its mark, turn the gate back over the reserve hub.
fidelity: Rigid boxes; rolls are 12-sided rings. Each hub turns on a free revolute joint; a release tab draws its sprung half in by a rule, not a linkage. The stub starts welded to its hub until the tab is pressed. Stay and latch are pre-made welds switched by rules. Tissue sheets are not simulated: the outlet windows and the changeover shutter are geometry and a sprung slide.
